extracted.intended_audience: applicants, agents, and national/ international patent offices and authorities handling PCT international applications (receiving Offices, International Searching Authorities, International Preliminary Examining Authorities, International Bureau)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards from the PCT Regulations and Manual governing rectification of mistakes, correspondence, communications, access to files, record-keeping, fees, and related procedures for international (PCT) patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent authority for rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: The rectification of a mistake shall be subject to authorization by the 'competent authority'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent authority depends on the part of the international application or document: (i) mistake in request part or correction thereof - receiving Office; (ii) mistake in description, claims or drawings or correction thereof - International Searching Authority (ISA), unless IPEA is competent under (iii); (iii) mistake in description, claims or drawings or in amendment under Article 19 or 34 where a demand for international preliminary examination has been made and not withdrawn and the date for IPE has passed - International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA); (iv) mistake in other documents submitted to RO, ISA, IPEA or IB (other than abstract or Article 19 amendment) - that Office/Authority/Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for authorization of rectification (obviousness test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent authority shall authorize the rectification of a mistake if, and only if, it is obvious to the competent authority that, as at the applicable date, something else was intended than what appears and that nothing else could have been intended than the proposed rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test is an objective 'obvious to the authority' standard evaluated as at the applicable date specified in Rule 91.1(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence considered for mistakes in description/claims/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For mistakes in the description, claims or drawings (or corrections/amendments thereof), the competent authority shall, for the purposes of the obviousness test, only take into account the contents of the description, claims and drawings and, where applicable, the correction or amendment concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External documents or file contents beyond the description/claims/drawings and the specific correction/amendment are excluded when assessing whether the rectification is obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence considered for mistakes in request part or other documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For mistakes in the request part of the international application or in documents referred to in Rule 91.1(b)(iv), the competent authority shall, for the purposes of the obviousness test, only take into account the contents of the international application itself and, where applicable, the correction concerned, the submitted document and any other document submitted with it, any available priority document in accordance with the Administrative Instructions, and any other document contained in the authority's international application file at the applicable date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the evidentiary basis for the obviousness inquiry to material within the application/file and submitted together with the relevant request or document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable date for assessing rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable date for the purposes of the obviousness test is: (i) for a mistake in a part of the international application as filed - the international filing date; (ii) for a mistake in a document other than the international application as filed (including a correction or amendment) - the date on which that document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines temporal point at which 'what was intended' is judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-rectifiable mistakes (general exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mistake shall not be rectifiable under Rule 91.1 if: (i) the mistake lies in omission of one or more entire elements of the international application (Article 3(2)) or entire sheets; (ii) the mistake is in the abstract; (iii) the mistake is in an amendment under Article 19, unless IPEA is competent; or (iv) the mistake is in a priority claim or notice correcting/adding a priority claim under Rule 26 bis.1(a) where rectification would change the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph notes that this does not affect operation of other specific Rules (20.4, 20.5, 26 bis and 38.3). These are hard exclusions where rectification is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to request rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an Office or Authority (RO, ISA, IPEA or IB) discovers what appears to be a rectifiable obvious mistake in the international application or another document, it may invite the applicant to request rectification under Rule 91.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authority-facilitated invitation is discretionary; it may prompt the applicant to file a formal rectification request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit and content of request for rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for rectification under Rule 91.1 shall be submitted to the competent authority within 26 months from the priority date and shall specify the mistake and the proposed rectification; it may contain a brief explanation at the applicant's option. Rule 26.4 applies mutatis mutandis as to how the proposed rectification shall be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 26-month deadline from priority date. The request must clearly identify the error and the exact change proposed; may include a short explanatory note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt decision and notification by competent authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent authority shall promptly decide whether to authorize or refuse rectification and shall promptly notify the applicant and the International Bureau of the authorization or refusal and, in case of refusal, give reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International Bureau then proceeds per Administrative Instructions, notifying receiving Offices, ISAs, IPEAs and designated/elected Offices as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorized rectification (implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where rectification of an obvious mistake has been authorized under Rule 91.1, the document concerned shall be rectified in accordance with the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions govern how the authorized change is to be implemented in the record and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness date of authorized rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized rectification shall be effective: (i) for a mistake in the international application as filed - from the international filing date; (ii) for a mistake in a document other than the international application as filed (including correction/amendment) - from the date on which that document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal effect backdates to filing date for mistakes in the filed application; for later documents, effective from their submission date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of refusal upon applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the competent authority refuses to authorize rectification, the International Bureau shall, upon request by the applicant within two months and subject to payment of a special fee, publish the request for rectification, the reasons for refusal and any further brief comments submitted by the applicant, if possible together with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the request, reasons and comments should, if possible, be included in Article 20 communications where the IA is not published under Article 64(3). This is a remedy for applicants to make a public record of disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office treatment of authorized rectification already in processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The rectification of an obvious mistake need not be taken into account by any designated Office in which processing or examination of the international application has already started prior to the date on which that Office is notified of the authorization of the rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices are not bound to apply the rectification if they began processing before being notified, subject to national practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Office power to disregard authorized rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office may disregard a rectification authorized under Rule 91.1 only if it finds that it would not have authorized the rectification under Rule 91.1 if it had been the competent authority, provided that the Office gives the applicant the opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time limit before disregarding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office must provide applicant chance to comment; the time limit must be reasonable under the circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter and signature requirement for correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper submitted by the applicant during the international procedure, other than the international application itself, shall, if not itself in the form of a letter, be accompanied by a letter identifying the international application to which it relates. The letter shall be signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures documents are clearly linked and authenticated. Applies to correspondence submitted to Offices/Authorities/Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy for missing letter or signature
rubrics_metrics.description: If the letter or signature requirements are not complied with, the applicant shall be informed and invited to remedy the omission within a time limit fixed in the invitation (not less than 10 days and not more than one month). If remedied within the time limit, the omission is disregarded; otherwise the paper is disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit must be reasonable even if it extends beyond the original time limit for furnishing the paper. Minimum and maximum specified to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlooked non-compliance disregarded if paper used
rubrics_metrics.description: Where non-compliance with the letter/signature requirements has been overlooked and the paper taken into account in the international procedure, the non-compliance shall be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a cure for administrative oversight where authorities already acted on the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of letters to ISA/IPEA and IB
rubrics_metrics.description: Any letter or document submitted by the applicant to the ISA or IPEA shall be in the same language as the international application, subject to certain Rules; where a translation has been transmitted or furnished, the language of that translation shall be used. A letter to ISA/IPEA may be in another language if the Authority authorizes it. Any letter from the applicant to the International Bureau shall be in English, French or any other language of publication permitted by the Administrative Instructions. Any letter or notification from the International Bureau to the applicant or to any national Office shall be in English or French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes default language rules and permitted exceptions; Authorities may authorize other languages by agreement or administrative instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing method by National Offices/IGOs (time-limit triggering events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document or letter emanating from a national Office or intergovernmental organization and constituting an event from the date of which any time limit under the Treaty/Regulations commences to run shall be sent by air mail, unless surface mail normally arrives within two days or air mail is not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures timely international mailings that trigger procedural time limits are sent by fast means except in specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and treatment of telegraph/teleprinter/facsimile/etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: A document making up the international application, and any later document or correspondence, may be transmitted by telegraph, teleprinter, facsimile machine or other like means, subject to conditions. A signature on a facsimile is recognized as proper. If part or all of a received transmitted document is illegible or missing, the document is treated as not received to the extent illegible or missing and the applicant shall be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission subject to Rule 11.14 and 92.1(a) and paragraph (h). Recognizes fax signatures; illegible/incomplete transmissions are treated as non-received to the extent defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to furnish original of transmitted document
rubrics_metrics.description: Any national Office or intergovernmental organization may require that the original of any document transmitted by telegraph/fax/etc. and an accompanying letter identifying that transmission be furnished within 14 days from transmission, provided that the requirement has been notified to the International Bureau and published in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification in Gazette must specify whether requirement concerns all or only certain kinds of documents. This allows Offices to insist on originals for evidentiary certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to furnish original when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant fails to furnish the original as required, the national Office or intergovernmental organization may: (i) waive the requirement; or (ii) invite the applicant to furnish the original within a reasonable time fixed in the invitation. If the document concerned is the international application and original is not furnished, the application shall be considered withdrawn; if a subsequent document, it shall be considered not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may also issue invitations to correct defects or proceed under other Rules. The response time must be reasonable and depends on document kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office need to notify IB before accepting electronic transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No national Office or intergovernmental organization shall be obliged to receive any document submitted by telegraph/teleprinter/fax/etc. unless it has notified the International Bureau that it is prepared to receive such documents and the IB has published information in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects Offices from being obliged to accept electronic/faxed transmissions unless they opt in and IB publishes the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording changes of applicant/agent/inventor by International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall, on request of the applicant or the receiving Office, record changes in person, name, residence, nationality or address of the applicant and changes in person, name or address of the agent, common representative or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB shall not record requested changes received after expiration of 30 months from the priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period for Receiving Office records
rubrics_metrics.description: Each receiving Office shall keep the records relating to each international application or purported international application, including the home copy, for at least 10 years from the international filing date or, where no international filing date is accorded, from the date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures national receiving Offices maintain application records for a minimum statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period for International Bureau records
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall keep the file, including the record copy, of any international application for at least 30 years from the date of receipt. The basic records of the International Bureau shall be kept indefinitely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB has longer-term archival obligations; core records are permanent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention period for ISA and IPEA files
rubrics_metrics.description: Each International Searching Authority and each International Preliminary Examining Authority shall keep the file of each international application it receives for at least 10 years from the international filing date and shall furnish, subject to reimbursement of cost, copies of any document contained in its file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISAs and IPEAs are required to retain files and provide copies on request (costs may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted forms of record-keeping (reproductions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records, copies and files may be kept as photographic, electronic or other reproductions, provided that the reproductions meet the obligations to keep records, copies and files under Rules 93.1 to 93.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows non-paper archival formats so long as they reliably preserve required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of documents by IB to designated/elected Offices (on request)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications by the International Bureau of an international application, notification, communication, correspondence or other document to any designated/elected Office shall be effected only upon request by the Office and at the time specified by that Office; requests may specify individual documents or classes of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB will deliver only what an Office requests and when requested; this governs inter-office electronic communications and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic availability considered communication time
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication is considered effected at the time when the International Bureau makes the document available to the designated/elected Office in electronic form in a digital library (where agreed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits IB to use an electronic retrieval model where Offices retrieve documents from an IB digital library; timing is when made available, not when retrieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to IB-held file (general rule and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the applicant or any person authorized by the applicant, the International Bureau shall furnish copies of any document contained in its file; at the request of any person, but not before international publication and subject to Article 38 and paragraphs (d) to (g), the IB shall furnish copies (possibly subject to reimbursement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access by third parties is restricted before publication and subject to rules protecting non-published/omitted material and internal-use documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: IB restrictions on access: omitted-from-publication material
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall not provide access to any information omitted from publication under Rule 48.2(l) or to any document relating to a request under that Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects information excluded from publication by Rule 48.2(l) from public access through IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: IB may withhold access upon reasoned applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a reasoned request by the applicant, the IB shall not provide access to any information in its file if it finds that: (i) the information does not obviously serve the purpose of informing the public about the IA; (ii) public access would clearly prejudice personal or economic interests of any person; and (iii) there is no prevailing public interest to have access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires IB assessment and offers applicant a protective avenue for withholding sensitive information; Rule 26.4 applies mutatis mutandis for presentation of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: IB will notify Offices when information omitted from public access is also in their files
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IB has omitted information from public access and that information is also contained in the file held by the receiving Office, ISA, Authority specified for supplementary search or IPEA, the IB shall promptly notify that Office/Authority accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent treatment across Offices when IB omits information from public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: IB will not provide access to IB internal-use documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall not provide access to any document contained in its file which was prepared solely for internal use by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal administrative documents are excluded from public access even after publication subject to other rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office access to its file
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the applicant or any person authorized by the applicant, the receiving Office may provide access to any document in its file. At the request of any person, but not before international publication and subject to limitation, the receiving Office may provide access to its file. The receiving Office shall not provide access to information it has been notified by the IB was omitted from publication or public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel rules to IB for RO-held files, with reimbursement for copies possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA access to its file
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the applicant or authorized person, the ISA may provide access to any document in its file. At the request of any person, but not before international publication and subject to limitation, the ISA may provide access. ISA shall not provide access to information omitted from publication or public access as notified by the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same limits apply to ISAs as to IB/RO with respect to omitted material and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA access to its file
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the applicant or authorized person, the IPEA shall provide access to any document in its file. At the request of any elected Office, but not before the international preliminary examination report is established and subject to limitation, the IPEA shall provide access. IPEA shall not provide access to information omitted from publication or public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elected Offices get access only after IPER is established; withheld material per IB notification remains protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated/Elected Office access governed by national law
rubrics_metrics.description: If national law applicable to a designated or elected Office allows access by third parties to a national file, that Office may allow access to documents relating to the international application to the same extent as provided by national law for a national application, but not before the earliest of dates in Article 30(2)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law determines third-party access at national stage, subject to PCT timing constraints; furnishing copies may be subject to reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and translations supplied by designated/elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated or elected Office shall notify the International Bureau within two months (or as soon as reasonably possible) of events such as: (i) date of performance of acts under Article 22 or 39 and any national application number assigned; (ii) if the Office explicitly publishes the IA under national law, the number and date of that national publication; (iii) where a patent is granted, the date of grant and, if IA is published in the form granted, the number and date of that national publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures IB receives timely info about national-stage events; notifications support global tracking of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated/elected Offices must provide IB with translations furnished to them; IB may furnish copies
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the International Bureau, any designated or elected Office shall provide it with a copy of the translation of the international application furnished by the applicant. The International Bureau may, upon request and subject to reimbursement of the cost, furnish to any person copies of the translations received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates access to translations through IB, subject to cost recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees: amounts and currency
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts of fees referred to in Rules 15, 45 bis.2 and 57 are expressed in Swiss currency and specified in the Schedule of Fees annexed to the Regulations. Example amounts: international filing fee: 1,330 CHF plus 15 CHF per sheet in excess of 30; supplementary search handling fee: 200 CHF; handling fee: 200 CHF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Schedule of Fees forms an integral part of the Regulations; exact amounts are set in the Schedule and may be updated by administrative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions for electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductions to the international filing fee apply if the international application is filed in electronic form: 100 CHF reduction where the request is not in character coded format; 200 CHF reduction where the request is in character coded format; 300 CHF reduction where request, description, claims and abstract are in character coded format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages electronic, machine-readable submissions by tiered reductions depending on the completeness of character-coded content.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90% fee reduction for applicants from low-GDP or least developed countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The international filing fee (as reduced where applicable), the supplementary search handling fee and the handling fee are reduced by 90% if the international application is filed by: (a) an applicant who is a natural person and is a national of and resides in a State listed as having per capita GDP below US$25,000 and whose nationals/residents have filed less than specified filing rates; or (b) an applicant (natural or not) who is a national of and resides in a State listed as a least developed country; provided that no beneficial owner fails the criteria and if several applicants each must satisfy the criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of eligible States are updated at least every five years by the Director General; criteria reviewed by the Assembly at least every five years; conditions apply when multiple applicants or beneficial owners exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and transfer of collected fees between Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a fee is collected by one Office (collecting Office) for the benefit of another Office (beneficiary Office), the collecting Office shall promptly notify the receipt of each fee in accordance with the Administrative Instructions. Upon receipt of notification, the beneficiary Office shall proceed as if it had received the fee on the date the collecting Office received it. The collecting Office shall transfer any fees collected for the benefit of a beneficiary Office to that Office in accordance with the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions govern notification and transfer mechanics; beneficiary Office's accounting acts from the collecting Office's receipt date.
